notes.ente: Une vache; un taureau is a bull.
notes.endiga: Un mouton; the plural is regular: des moutons.
notes.ntya: Avoir peur de: j’ai peur du chien, j’ai peur de la nuit.
notes.waliwo: Il y a: never changes, for one thing or many.
notes.kkapa: Un chat; a female cat is une chatte.
notes.engaali: La grue couronnée, Uganda’s national bird.
notes.hakuna-matata: Pas de souci, or pas de problème.

guidebook.intro: Name farm animals, wild animals and pets. French plurals have some surprises, and fear takes “de”.

tips.title: Animal, animaux
body: Nouns ending in **-al** usually change to **-aux** in the plural: **un animal, des animaux; un cheval, des chevaux**. Nouns ending in **-eau** add **-x**: **un oiseau, des oiseaux**.
As with **-s**, you don’t hear the **-x**: **oiseau** and **oiseaux** sound the same.

tips.title: J’ai peur du serpent
body: Fear uses **avoir peur de** (to have fear of): **J’ai peur des lions.** **De + le** becomes **du** and **de + les** becomes **des**: **J’ai peur du serpent.**
**Il y a** (there is/are) and its negative **il n’y a pas de**: **Il y a des girafes. Il n’y a pas d’eau.**

culture.title: Animals in stories
body: In West African tales, the clever hero is often **Leuk le lièvre** (the hare), and the foolish one **Bouki l’hyène**. Sounds familiar? In Buganda, the hare **Wakayima** plays the same trickster role.
